comments.body:
**medium** · `tests-and-dependencies` check

`test_callable_max_uses_bounds_local_consultations_across_runs` only changes the deps budget between the two `agent.run` calls (this line, after the first run has finished) and consults at most once per run. With `max_uses=lambda ctx: 3 - ctx.deps.used` and `used=2`, both the new `prepare`-based limit and a naive per-call `self._max_uses_for(ctx)` read produce exactly one consultation followed by the limit message, so the test (and the existing int `max_uses` tests, which use a constant limit) cannot tell them apart. That leaves the local half of this change unpinned: `_prepare_local`'s stated contract ("Fix the local limit once per request, so parallel calls share it") and the PR body's claim that a caller counter updated while calls run cannot make the last allowed call refuse itself. A change that drops `prepare` and resolves the callable inside `advisor()` would keep every existing and new test green. Fix: have `advisor_model` increment `budget.used` once per consultation so the parallel calls in one request observe a moving value, and assert all three calls allowed by the limit fixed at request start still consult (e.g. start at `used=0`, expect three consultations rather than the two a per-call read would permit).

<!-- pr-review-checks finding=f9462a5ce689ffb51e519fec5403f8299c6ef30073475ba3b9c30d4622bc3e1e -->

Agreed. Fixed in stacked #13659: the advisor model now spends from the shared budget during the run and the calls run sequentially, so a per-call read would allow one consultation where the prepare-time limit allows two. Confirmed the test fails with the limit read inside the tool body.
